notes.title: New Locomotion, Blocking, and Fake Snaps - July Title Update
notes.content:
[p]What’s up, Maximum Football fans! [/p][p]We are excited to publish our first major update to Maximum Football since launching into 1.0 last month. This update includes a number of bug fixes, gameplay improvements, and feature updates designed to address some of the main points of feedback we’ve been hearing from the community since  1.0 launch. [/p][p]In our most recent Dev Blog, we shared that a new CPU playcalling system was in the works. During testing over the past week, we identified several areas that need further refinement. To ensure it meets our standards and delivers the best experience, we’ve decided to move the release of this feature to the August update.[/p][p]Here’s what’s included in the update. [/p][h2][b]New Locomotion[/b][/h2][previewyoutube="irTmni1o1D8;full"][/previewyoutube][p]We’ve continued our work on refining player movement to make gameplay feel smoother, more responsive, and more lifelike. This update includes several key changes to how players move on the field:[/p][list][*][p][b]Speed-Based Animations:[/b] Players now transition more naturally between movement speeds. As a player accelerates, their running animations update to match—limbs move faster, and strides lengthen to reflect the pace.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improved Transitions:[/b] We’ve smoothed out the transitions between idle and movement, especially when changing directions. This is most noticeable on screen plays and short routes—where previously, receivers would hesitate after catching the ball. Now, they’ll fluidly transition into their next movement, getting upfield more quickly and realistically.[/p][/*][/list][p]These updates are part of our ongoing effort to make every movement—from a quick cut to a breakaway run—feel as clean and satisfying as possible.[/p][h2][b]Updated Pass Blocking[/b][/h2][p]Blocking has been a key area of focus leading into 1.0, and while earlier updates improved run blocking and special teams performance, this update zeroes in on [b]pass protection[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]Pocket Formation Improvements:[/b] Offensive linemen are now better at forming and maintaining the pocket. Rather than chasing defenders out of position, they focus on threats directly in front of them—helping to seal off interior gaps and reinforce the wall around the quarterback.[/p][/*][*][p][b]QB-Aware Blocking Logic:[/b] Linemen now have improved awareness of the quarterback’s movement. They’ll work to steer pass rushers away from the QB’s current position, helping reduce pressure from blindside or broken-pocket scenarios.[/p][/*][/list][p]These changes are designed to create a more realistic and reliable pass protection experience—and give your quarterback the time they need to make the right throw.[/p][h2][b]Fake Snap[/b][/h2][p]You can now use a fake snap to keep the defense guessing.[/p][list][*][p]Tap RB (Xbox) / R1 (PlayStation) at the line of scrimmage to perform a hard count.[/p][/*][*][p]Use it to try and draw the defense offsides or disrupt their timing before the snap.[/p][/*][/list][p]Mix this into your pre-snap routine to gain an edge against aggressive defenders.
[/p][h2][b]Full Patch Notes[/b][/h2][h3]Here’s what else is included in this month’s update:

notes.title: Maximum Football 1.0 Arrives June
notes.content:
Mark your calendars: Maximum Football officially launches into 1.0 on June 17 

After launching into Steam Early Access and Xbox Game Preview last year, we’ve delivered over a dozen updates and hotfixes to improve gameplay, enhance quality of life, and expand the game's core features. From Coach Mode and couch multiplayer to invite-based online play and full Dynasty spectating, many of the most impactful additions came directly from your feedback. 

[previewyoutube=qgcqn2AZp0M;full][/previewyoutube]

Now, we’re gearing up for the next chapter. On June 17, we leave Early Access behind and take our biggest step yet—with new features, new players, and a brand-new season of content. But before we kick things off, let’s take a look at what 1.0 means for the future of Maximum Football. 

[h2]What Does 1.0 Mean [/h2]

Reaching 1.0 is a major milestone—but it’s far from the finish line. Launching out of Early Access means we can bring Maximum Football to new players and platforms, while continuing to refine the core gameplay and deliver the features our community has asked for. 

Development isn’t slowing down. We’ll keep pushing regular updates, introducing new features, and expanding the game with fresh content. Our goal is to make Maximum Football the ultimate sandbox for building your dream football experience. 

Now, let’s dive into what’s coming with the 1.0 launch. 

[h2]New Features [/h2]

[h3]Maximum Football on PlayStation 5! [/h3]

You’ve been asking—and we’re thrilled to deliver. With the 1.0 launch, Maximum Football is officially coming to PlayStation 5. Starting June 17, PlayStation players can finally join in and start building their ultimate football universe. 

[h3]Weather[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/d23c458dd07359bf5b3f70c10d3a88fb71fda257.jpg[/img]
Until now, every game has taken place under clear skies. That changes with 1.0. Rain and snow are being added to Maximum Football, bringing new atmosphere and challenge to your gameday experience.  

[h3]Stadium Customization [/h3]

Make your stadium a true reflection of your team’s identity. With the 1.0 launch, you’ll be able to personalize your field color and stadium seating to match your team’s branding. It’s your home—make it look the part. 

[h3]Multiple Team Logos [/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/5b437b61e4682a0e7850693547df6657db3362d5.jpg[/img]
College football teams don’t stop at just one logo—and now, neither do you. With 1.0, you can upload up to nine logos per team and use them across your uniforms. Build a brand that feels as dynamic as the team you’ve created. 

[h3]Season 3 [/h3]

June 17 doesn’t just mark the launch of 1.0—it also kicks off a brand-new season of content (we’ll reveal the full theme soon!). We’re using your feedback to improve how Season Pass content is earned and what’s included. 

First, in addition to weekly and seasonal challenges, we’re introducing passive XP—you’ll now make progress on your Season Pass just by finishing games. Play your way and keep moving forward. 

We’re also expanding the rewards on both the free and premium tracks. That includes more variety, higher-value items, and not one, but two stadiums: 

[list]
[*] The premium reward at Tier 1 gives pass holders a brand-new stadium right from the start. 
[*] The free reward at Tier 50 offers a second stadium for all players who complete the pass. 
[/list]
[h3]Updated Animations and Anatomy [/h3]
We’re packing in a wide range of new animations for 1.0, including an updated kickoff sequence and improvements to catching, running, and tackling. You’ll also notice non-gameplay animations—players reacting on the sidelines, motioning between plays, and more—that bring added life and immersion to every snap. 

Beyond animations, we’ve refined how player bodies respond to the action. Players now move more naturally, track plays with greater awareness, and interact with each other more believably during collisions and transitions. 

But enough talk—you want to see this in action! Come back next Tuesday for a full half of 1.0 gameplay IN THE SNOW!

[h2]FAQs[/h2]

[h3]1. What game modes will be available on June 17th?[/h3]

On June 17th, you will be able to play Exhibition Mode, Dynasty, Maximum Pro League, Couch Multiplayer, Coach Mode, and Invite Multiplayer, as well as create teams in the Maximum Football Customization Suite.

[h3]2. What platforms will Maximum Football be available on when it releases on June 17th?[/h3]

Maximum Football will be available to play on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.

[h3]3. What editions of the game will be available?[/h3]

[b]Base Game (Free):[/b]
[list]
[*] Maximum Pro League
[*] Single Player Exhibition Mode
[*] Customization Suite
[*] Dynasty Starter Mode (Free Access to initial seasons)
[/list]
[b]Dynasty Edition ($19.99):[/b]
[list]
[*] Base Game
[*] Unlimited Access to Dynasty Mode
[*] Dynasty Pack (Dynasty gloves, helmet, pants, mask, and fireball celebration)
[/list]
[b]Legend Edition ($39.99):[/b]
[list]
[*] Base Game
[*] Unlimited Dynasty Access and Dynasty Pack
[*] Unlimited Franchise Access and Franchise Pack (Coming in 2025)
[*] Legend Pack (Legend stadium, mouthguard, 1200 max stacks, and knee drop celebration)
[/list]

[h3]4. Is Franchise releasing with 1.0?[/h3]

Franchise won’t be available on June 17th. We are taking a bit more time to get it right. Be on the lookout for more information about Franchise later this summer.

[h3]5. Will crossplay be available on June 17th?[/h3]

No. In order to ensure the most stable online performance on launch day, crossplay will not be available. Crossplay will be added to the game in a future update.

[h3]6. Is the game still planned for release on PS4 and Xbox One?[/h3]

Yes!

[h3]7. Does the team still plan to release regular updates now that the game is in 1.0?[/h3]

Absolutely! 1.0 is the beginning of the next chapter of Maximum Football, and the feedback we receive from our existing community, returning players, and newcomers to Maximum Football will continue to shape the future of this game.

notes.title: Dev Blog: Weather, Stadium Customization, and Blocking
notes.content:
What’s going on, Maximum Football crew!  

Luke here from the Maximum Football team, kicking off a new regular check-in series where we break down what we’re working on—and what you can look forward to in Maximum Football. 

These check-ins are a way for us to pull back the curtain and bring you deeper into our development process. Maximum Football is a game being shaped by its community, and we want to keep that collaboration going strong. 

[h2]What We’re Working On [/h2]
Last week, we launched our first major patch of Season 2. We’ve received ample feedback from you – thank you for sharing your suggestions.  

[h3]MPL Depth Chart Issues [/h3]
We saw some reports of users who encountered a bug where they got duplicate versions of their MPL cards. 

We identified the source of this issue and pushed a hotfix for this bug this week.   

[h3]Blocking Improvements [/h3]
We made a lot of adjustments to blocking in our most recent patch, and we’ve seen from the community that this has been a big improvement over the way the game played pre-patch. However, we are still seeing lingering issues especially on special teams  that we want to address in our next update. Blocked punts and blocked FGs are still happening at too high a rate for our liking, and we want to continue to make changes to improve the effectiveness of special teams.  

[h3]Chasing down some lingering clock issues [/h3]
Our hotfix last week addressed a number of clock issues that players were encountering following the patch. However, we are still monitoring a few player reports of lingering clock issues. If you see any weird behavior from the clock, please drop it in the comments or in our #Feedback channel on Discord.  

[h2]Looking Ahead [/h2]
We recently announced that Maximum Football is coming to PlayStation 5 this summer—and our team is hard at work preparing for that launch. That means polishing core gameplay and introducing features that will debut with the 1.0 release. 

[h3]Weather Effects [/h3]

Rain and snow are on the horizon! As mentioned in a previous mailbag, cosmetic weather will be added for 1.0. This will be a visual-only update to start, with gameplay-affecting weather planned for later this year.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/cbe335770e5c83315dffcf5c339a21ec47bd39c9.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/7eac18dffe37b9ff66e1b555c2a251261575ed3b.jpg[/img]

[h3]New Playcalling System [/h3]
Football is about the Jimmies and the Joes, but it is also about the X’s and the O’s. And we are hard at work on a new playcalling system that is going to add a new layer of realism to CPU coaching. This system is going to help address several areas that we’ve heard community feedback on including: 
[list]
[*] Late game playcalling and awareness 
[*] Run and pass balance 
[*] Defensive playcalling
[/list]
We have this system currently working on our development build, but before we release it out to the public, we have a very simple philosophy -- “is this better than the system that we currently have.” Until we can answer that with a resounding yes, we are going to continue to polish it.  

[h3]Stadium Customization[/h3]
Customization is a pillar of Maximum Football. We want to give players the tools they need to make the teams they want to make. The next addition we are making to that end is the ability to customize the color of the turf and the seats in your stadium. From various natural grass colors to vibrant artificial turf, you will soon be able to express your style in brand new ways in Maximum Football.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/66b1b93563c1fd9d968e8386d0f0728f78b7355e.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/0ff85b5fc234a66fae830fdb9fecf3524d5799e6.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/9a4504115579f25fe57aefd7b6b5bd354dfb4668.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/9c45c4aa07bcce9df7d8d1840b90a84f932440c6.jpg[/img]

[h2]Mailbag: Your Questions, Answered [/h2]
In the past, we have done monthly mailbags, giving you all the opportunity to submit your questions for the development team to answer. Now, we want to answer your questions more regularly, so we will be adding a Q&A as a part of these Dev Blogs!  

So, drop your questions in the comments below or in the #Monthly-Mailbag channel in our Discord, and we may choose to answer them in our next Dev Blog.  

[h2]In Case You Missed It [/h2]
Last week’s patch focused on stabilizing key areas of gameplay and introduced a long-requested feature from the community. Here’s what’s in the latest patch: 
[list]
[*] Couch Multiplayer – Face off with friends on the same console and battle it out for bragging rights. 
[*] Offensive Line Fixes – We’ve tackled several issues that made blocking feel underpowered. Both pass protection and run blocking should now feel more balanced and consistent. 
[*] Offsides Penalties – The invisible wall at the line of scrimmage is gone. Jump the snap early? That’s an offsides. 
[*] Hurry-Up Offense – Run a fast-paced offense with the new hurry-up functionality—perfect for two-minute drills or keeping defenses on their heels. 
[*] Gameplay Sliders – We're introducing an experimental feature that lets you tweak gameplay to your liking. Sliders will be available in Exhibition and Exhibition Coach Mode only for now. 
[/list]
You can check out the full patch notes here. We also released two subsequent hotfixes to address things like a spectate bug, an issue with pump fakes, and reincluding day/night selection.

Hello, Maximum Football community!

Today we’ve released a hotfix on Steam and Xbox to resolve an issue affecting Spectate mode. CPU vs. CPU matches can now be watched without interruption.

[list]

[*] Unintended clock behavior in specific game situations
[*] Day/night options not appearing
[/list]

If you encounter the pump‑fake bug before tomorrow’s update, simply attempt another pump fake (hold LT + a receiver icon). This will reset the quarterback’s animation and allow normal passing.

Thank you for your ongoing feedback and patience. We’re committed to making Maximum Football the best it can be—stay tuned for more improvements!

— The Maximum Football Team

notes.title: Couch Multiplayer, Updated Blocking and More Now Available
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

Thank you for continuing to support Maximum Football! Since the launch of Season 2: Vice Blitz, we’ve been blown away by your passion, gameplay clips, and honest feedback. Your input helps us shape the future of the game, and this latest patch is a direct result of your voices being heard. 

Today, we are releasing the first patch of the season. Let’s dive into some of the biggest improvements coming your way: 

[h2]️🛋️ Couch Multiplayer Is Here[/h2]
Grab a friend and settle the score locally—you can now play head-to-head on the same system. Whether you're going head-to-head in a rivalry game or testing out team builds, Couch Multiplayer is finally live. 

[h2]🧱 Offensive Line Fixes (Thanks to You!) [/h2]
We heard your frustration loud and clear: the O-line was getting bullied. Defensive linemen were breaking through far too easily, wrecking the run game and collapsing the pocket in seconds. 

This patch delivers improved offensive line play—giving you more time to survey the field and execute your gameplan. It’s a better balance between offense and defense, and a huge quality-of-life change that came directly from community feedback 

[h2]🚫 Offsides Penalties Are Now Live [/h2]
The era of running at the line pre-snap without consequences is over. Jumping the snap will now result in an offsides penalty, especially cracking down on online players who were abusing the invisible wall to gain an unfair edge. 

Clean up your timing—or be prepared to march backward. 

[h2]🏃‍♂️ Hurry-Up Offense [/h2]
Add some tempo to your attack! You can now run a no-huddle offense by holding Y after the play. Your squad will hustle to the line, giving you the chance to catch the defense off guard and keep drives alive. 

Those are the biggest highlights—but we’ve packed this patch with a lot more. Keep reading for the full list of detailed patch notes below. 

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
We are aware of an issue in this patch that is causing users to pump fake and lose the ability to pass. The team is working on a hot fix that will address this issue ASAP, and we will post an announcement when it is available. 

There are a few other known issues present in this build that we will fix in a future update. 
[list]
[*] some issues with the controller assignment for the 2nd user for couch play
[*] users may encounter an error when trying to access MPL; this gets fixed with a game restart
[*] there are some issues with registering the loss when disconnecting from an online ranked match
[/list]

[list]
[*] Onside kicks now work reliably even if you call a timeout after setting kick power, and crash‑related uniform syncing when joining sessions has been fixed. 
[*] Drill exercises (pass defense, hot routes, etc.) no longer get stuck after touchdown catches or when selecting plays. 
[*] Recovered‑punt touchdowns now correctly award possession 
[*] Star‑player indicator logic has been added. 
[*] Penalties are now observed by the rules engine, and AI will decline unnecessary penalties when they cost more yards. 
[*] “No‑Huddle” offenses and hurry‑up sequences no longer leave players in awkward formations or teleport defensive players. 
[*] Client‑side join logic was fixed so switching into coach mode—and other lobby privileges—don’t reset unexpectedly. 
[*] Exhibition‑mode stats challenges now track correctly (including two‑point conversions, missed kicks, and challenge progress), and match history statistics have been cleaned up. 
[*] Conversion kicks that miss no longer trigger a touchback, and delay‑of‑game positioning on extra‑point tries is now accurate. 
[*] Sideline players and coaches react dynamically—with animations and head‑tracking—to real‑time events like big plays and injuries. 
[*] Overtime coach suggestions now respect whether you’re allowed a conversion kick, and the new overtime ruleset is available in menu settings. 
[*] The play clock pauses during instant replays and auto‑rewind, with correct timing after turnovers and penalties (40 seconds NCAA, 25 seconds Pro). 
[*] Substitutions, depth‑chart views, and challenge‑system upgrades have been revamped: 
[*] Substitution panels now initialize properly. 
[*] Challenge values never go negative, and quest requirements update dynamically. 
[*] “Fair catch,” “pickup,” and “block” actions on punts are now handled correctly by both AI and user, and special hot‑route pass‑block options were added. 
[*] The profanity filter has been expanded and whitelist fixes applied. 
[*] Post‑play cameras now offer multiple perspectives, and you can disable auto‑replay if you prefer. 
[*] Controller LED flashes, input handling during cinematics, and UI prompts (e.g., waiting‑for‑match, error pop‑ups) have been polished to avoid duplicates or misfires. 
[*] Practice‑mode improvements include stable previous‑play selection, non‑conflicting keybinds, and accurate replay behavior when skipping cut‑scenes. 
[*] Demo/test features were added for QA (e.g., forced practice‑map states, debug property flags) to facilitate easier testing of new match conditions. 
[/list]

[list]
[*] Tweaked the new “strider” movement animations and added smooth blendspaces for it. 
[*] Introduced a set of new coach animations. 
[*] Added various sideline behaviors  
[*] Updated block‑engagement montages in the animation database for smoother look. 
[*] Added notifies and sync markers to all new strider animations for better timing. 
[*] Motion‑matching is now applied to all passing animations for more natural movement. 
[*] Refined the sprint animation based on design feedback. 
[*] Added new jump and 360‑turn catch animations to diversify receptions. 
[*] Adjusted open‑field blocking animations to look more dynamic. 
[*] Implemented diagonal QB movement animations so quarterbacks can move and pass on the run. 
[*] Polished several of the new catch animations and ensured they use the correct montage slots. 
[*] Fine‑tuned scramble (QB run) animations for better realism. 
[*] Introduced multiple new catch variations (CatchRun series and pump‑fake animations). 
[*] Slowed down post‑touchdown celebration animations for dramatic effect. 
[*] Improved sideline “messing with shoulder pads” and “helmet” idle behaviors on the bench. 
[*] Refined stationary QB and passing animations to blend more smoothly into movement. 
[*] Fixed bone‑orientation issues in kick‑catch animations so feet and hands align correctly. 
[*] Added quick‑pass variants and modified several existing quick‑pass animations. 
[*] Updated referee animations, including signals and idle behaviors. 
[*] Added “disappointment” animations for dropped catches.

[*] Added a number of new stadium cinematics.

[*] Improved navigation so menu focus never gets stuck while moving through dynasty screens. 
[*] Applied general performance and stability fixes tied to dynasty progression and milestone events.

[*] Blocked user inputs during dynasty loading screens to prevent accidental selections and refined achievement tracking for “Match” and “Changed Up.”

[*] Fixed various matchmaking errors that could recreate sessions incorrectly when offline. 
[*] Removed duplicate team options in ranked matchmaking. 
[*] Added two‑point conversion tracking for challenge progress. 
[*] Restored access to team‑option settings during MPL matchmaking. 
[*] Recorded match state on disconnects so abandoned games and penalties apply correctly. 
[*] Prevented matchmaking from advertising joinable sessions once you’ve left the queue. 
[*] Ensured presence information is correctly disabled during matchmaking. 
[*] Stopped penalty from firing improperly when accepting an invitation in queue. 
[*] Enabled alternate uniforms in MPL matches against the CPU. 
[*] Improved disconnect handling for hosts and clients, logging errors when sessions drop. 
[*] Fixed the “No Contest” prompt so it only appears once per player. 
[*] Allowed client users to trigger no‑huddle offense in MP matches. 
[*] Tweaked the penalization process to apply the right penalties in all cases. 
[*] Resolved issues where the rank‑up panel would fail to open. 
[*] Fixed errors in match‑loss recording when a disconnect happens. 
[*] Improved error handling when retrieving first‑time card rewards and suppressed “no reward” cases on disconnect. 
[*] Ensured the matchmaking UI deactivates properly once you leave the lobby. 
[*] Corrected leaderboard sorting and profile name references. 
[*] Added error handlers for client justice events and host quits. 
[*] Cleaned up misleading UI messages when a client disconnects from a hosted match. 
[*] Fixed starting kit assignment in MPL. 
[*] Refactored initial card object setup to run during challenge initialization. 
[/list]
[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
[list]
[*] Ensured custom team uniforms replicate correctly for all players online. 
[*] Enabled “Coach Mode” features to work properly in online exhibition matches. 
[*] After joining via an invite, restored permissions callbacks so you retain host or VIP privileges. 
[*] Prevented the host from being disconnected when an opponent quits an online exhibition (disconnects only apply in MPL). 
[*] Separated the grid layout and invite button so they no longer overlap or conflict. 
[*] Fixed local‑multiplayer banners so Player 1 and Player 2 show correctly in‑game. 
[*] Corrected star‑player tagging and rating calculations in multiplayer games. 
[*] Streamlined the local‑multiplayer replay start and finish flow, with corresponding UI tweaks. 
[*] Properly tear down online sessions at game end, and removed unnecessary penalty and error pop‑ups afterward. 
[*] Cleaned up sessions when network connectivity is lost to avoid lingering or broken connections. 
[*] Delayed initial session creation to prevent friends from joining too early during matchmaking. 
[/list]
[h2]Customization[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed the mouthguard silhouette so it uses the correct material slot. 
[*] Ensured the “Alternate Uniform” button hides when you’re in player customization. 
[*] Corrected an issue where away teams sometimes showed the wrong uniform. 
[*] Adjusted cleat patterns so they display correctly. 
[*] Fine‑tuned the position of logos on pants. 
[*] Fixed the secondary UV mapping channel on the primary jersey mesh. 
[*] Added realistic dirt mask textures for gloves, helmets, wrist wraps, and finger tape. 
[*] Prevented custom logos from being validated multiple times in the same session to speed things up. 
[*] Made page‑left and page‑right thumbstick inputs move between custom logo pages. 
[*] Switched roster and team loading to fully asynchronous so custom teams and rosters load more reliably. 
[*] Updated the dirt‑application shader to pull data from the correct source, and added mouthguards to replay characters. 
[*] Fixed filter logic in the player customization browser so items show and hide correctly. 
[*] Corrected helmet pattern IDs so every design displays as intended. 
[*] Made sure the “Select Uniform” option keeps focus when navigating menus. 
[*] Fixed uniform names so they display properly in multiplayer team‑select screens. 
[*] Added context‑sensitive buttons for switching to alternate uniforms only when appropriate. 
[*] Mapped “Apply Uniform To All Players” and “Reset To Team Default” to the special-left controller button. 
[*] Fixed a pants‑logo mirroring bug so logos don’t flip unexpectedly. 
[/list]

[*] Added freshly recorded quarterback calls to the game. 
[*] Corrected the halftime “first down” commentary, which was triggering incorrectly when you started offense to begin the second half. 
[*] Made sure that when a quarterback scores a touchdown by running, it’s announced as a rushing TD. 
[*] Added newly recorded quarterback calls and polished their sound effects. 
[*] Prevented slide commentary from playing when the QB actually dives near the goal line. 
[*] Improved two‑point conversion voice lines: 
[*] No longer calls it “unsuccessful” if the runner is tackled in the end zone. 
[*] Still calls it “unsuccessful” on an incomplete pass. 
[*] Tweaked certain commentary lines to use “he” and avoid repeating player names too often. 
[*] Added a system to filter out inappropriate or duplicate commentary lines based on metadata before playback. 
[*] Adjusted the passing commentary for deep throws (“DeepPass”) and quick releases (“QuickPass”), and updated related animations. 
[*] Added weight‑training conversation 
[*] Tagged individual commentary lines with metadata to support smoother flow in upcoming features. 
[*] Improved audible related commentary. 
[*] Commentator now calls out an audible only once per down. 
[*] Player chatter for audibles now uses multiple voice actors, randomly chosen at game start and then kept consistent. 
[*] Finished adding and fixing get‑up celebration sounds and their animations. 
[*] Added a slight delay to audible commentary so it lines up better with player movement, and refined tackle and sack voice lines. 
[*] Fixed several mistriggered calls around punts, sacks, and slides—especially near the end zone—and updated the underlying database. 
[*] Enabled voice lines for time‑outs for both teams. 
[*] Added new variations of Dan’s juke, spin, and truck commentary lines. 
[*] Stopped “start of down” voice lines from firing too close to the goal line (so they don’t clash with “down and goal” lines). 
[*] Prevented “good run” commentary from playing on plays that lose yardage or end in turnovers. 
[*] Reorganized “down and goal” voice calls so Dan always responds to Garrett. 
[*] Added and refined penalty timing voice lines (e.g. “badly timed penalty”). 
[*] Merged some redundant commentary events (e.g. removing “yard‑line touchdown” in favor of existing kick‑return touchdown calls). 
[*] Updated voice calls for field‑goal formations, kickoffs, tackles, and catches. 
[*] Refactored how “down” and “goal” calls work so they only run on their specific downs. 
[*] Enabled the special “goal for the win” voice line when you’re kicking to win the game. 
[*] Added and fixed play‑clock commentary responses. 
[*] Updated open‑field detach and run‑to animations with matching voice lines. 
[*] Added voice calls for punts, onside kicks, punt returns, and QB slides. 
[*] Added voice lines for catch‑and‑run failures, fake‑pass reactions, and slowed plays. 
[*] Improved commentary cross‑fading by using two audio channels so that one line can begin fading in as the previous is fading out. 
[*] Allowed different punt commentary for fourth downs versus other downs. 
[*] Added general “filler” commentary that triggers during prolonged gameplay, unrelated to specific events. 
[*] Fixed a variety of multiplayer commentary issues (character abilities, touchdowns, tackles, downs, and kicks). 
[*] Recorded a new positive catch reaction from Garrett and adjusted the database. 
[*] Fixed ambiance‑toggle sounds and improved pre‑snap, pass, and audible sound effects. 
[*] Added voice lines for offsides and kick‑return variations. 
[*] Finalized and polished the “Practice Field” stadium reverb effect. 
[*] Squashed a popping UI sound. 
[*] Improved the natural flow of commentary by tracking the current speaker—allowing cross‑fades only between different speakers. 
[*] Added and refined dozens of voice lines for goal‑post hits, extra points, snap announcements, and more, including animations like block‑running, fake‑handoff, and handoff‑catch. 
[/list]
[h2]UI[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added visual indicators for the star player and “Read Key Defender” markers. 
[*] Prevented navigation from inadvertently “escaping” off the discard pack screen. 
[*] Fixed an edge case in Exhibition mode where the team‑selection panel could get out of sync when switching sides. 
[*] Standardized terminology throughout the Settings menu. 
[*] Moved the Defensive Hot Route (DHR) controls to the left side for Player 2 and hid pre‑snap buttons when they’re not needed. 
[*] Ensured that in local multiplayer, opening the playbook keeps focus on the Team Selection hub instead of losing it. 
[*] Displayed the Read Key defender icon in the HUD when appropriate. 
[*] Show user avatars only when every team on screen is controlled by a human player. 
[*] When one player pauses, suspended input and hid unnecessary layers for the other local player. 
[*] Prevented the “Hurry back to line” prompt from appearing in spectator mode. 
[*] Added player avatar widgets to both the in‑game scoreboard and floating indicators above panels. 
[*] Made sure guest profiles download and display their avatars correctly on all platforms. 
[*] Simplified guest player profiles in local multiplayer so they show a placeholder state when no custom avatar is set. 
[*] Collapsed the local‑player indicator in the Settings panel when it’s not needed, and fixed it showing up in the main menu. 
[*] Added consistent pause‑menu indicators for each player and their submenus, all driven by player data. 
[*] Enabled team option buttons on the matchmaking panel as soon as you open it for the selected side. 
[*] Improved how custom team logos load by checking for existing textures first and renaming new ones appropriately. 
[*] Updated the shop flags and fixed the Trade‑Up pack button so it says “Back” instead of “Buy another pack.” 
[*] Disabled side‑switch entries and footer buttons wherever a sub‑panel is active, preventing accidental clicks. 
[*] Disabled the decoy play suggestion during kickoffs when it doesn’t apply. 
[*] Added confirmation pop‑ups in the MPL menu when Casual or Unranked matchmaking is already in progress. 
[*] Restored focus handling in create‑team states so the “Select” button always appears. 
[*] Tweaked gameplay sliders and their input handling so values don’t jump unexpectedly and focus never gets lost. 
[*] Ensured the Broadcast Camera UI only shows if all players are in coach mode. 
[*] Updated background art for the Account Linking screen (including changing jersey numbers to 25). 
[*] Refreshed icons and text for season‑pass tutorials and end‑screen flows. 
[*] Fixed popup and leaderboard UI bugs: rank badges, season names, missing ranks, and connection overlays. 
[*] Renamed the “Motions” drill category to match design specs and added category filters to the drill selection screen. 
[*] Corrected textures for card‑pack and stadium‑grass UI elements. 
[*] Made new rank badges and updated drill lists to follow the design’s defined order rather than save order. 
[*] Prevented the connection error overlay from covering existing pop‑ups. 
[*] Saved team‑color changes reliably across sessions. 
[*] Updated the pants‑pattern index so your uniform choices always display correctly. 
[*] Hid the floating help widget during temporary button prompts. 
[*] Improved commentary‑slider widgets to prevent stuck hover animations and fixed deep‑press UI focus loss. 
[*] Reworked the season‑pass panel so the “Claim All” function refreshes immediately and shows a “Last Chance” banner on the buy button when you’re near the end of the pass. 
[*] Added new Audible UI controls and fine‑tuned input timing on the “Hurry Up” hold action. 
[*] Fixed focus issues when replay or debug windows open, and ensured pop‑ups suspend the correct player’s controls. 
[*] Updated the screenshot‑maker scene and page‑turner dots for smoother navigation. 
[*] Redesigned team logos throughout the menus. 
[*] Wired in the backend for the “Claim All” season‑pass button, and set gamepad inputs so they don’t conflict with other actions.
[*] Hid in‑game UI for Player 2 in local multiplayer end‑game screens. 
[/list]

notes.title: Welcome to Season 2: Vice Blitz
notes.content:
Last season, you took to the field aboard the iconic Aircraft Carrier Stadium. This time, we’re bringing the action to the sunny shores of the coastal Southeast. Get ready to suit up on the lime green turf of Seaside Park, a brand-new stadium surrounded by palm trees and coastal vibes. 

[previewyoutube=j9oyxpWOTkE;full][/previewyoutube]

But Season 2 isn’t just about a fresh backdrop and new cosmetics—we’ve also made meaningful changes based on your feedback. Progression is now faster, more flexible, and even more rewarding, making it easier to earn the content you want while playing the way you enjoy. 

As always, the Season Pass includes both free and premium rewards at every tier, featuring card packs, cosmetics, celebrations, and in-game currency. And don’t worry—if you decide to upgrade to the premium pass later in the season, you’ll instantly unlock any premium rewards you would have earned thanks to your progression. 

[h2]Changes To Progress in Season 2 [/h2]

We’ve made some adjustments to the way progression works in Season 2 based on feedback from the community. This season, you’ll earn rewards more quickly and have greater flexibility when it comes to completing challenges across different game modes. 

Let’s start with progression. In Season 1, we heard that some challenges felt a bit too specific or demanding, which made it harder for some players to stay on track. For Season 2, we’ve fine-tuned the difficulty of weekly and seasonal challenges to make them more approachable—so you can keep moving forward and unlocking rewards at a steady pace. 

We’re also expanding how and where you can complete challenges. Now, your stats will count toward weekly and seasonal progress whether you’re playing online or offline MPL, Dynasty mode, or Exhibition Mode. However you choose to play, your progress will follow. 

[h2]Defensive Hot Routes [/h2]

We’re adding more control to the defensive side of the ball in Season 2 with the introduction of defensive hot routes. You can now adjust individual defender assignments pre-snap, giving you the tools to counter what you’re seeing from the offense in real time. Whether you want to put a linebacker into a hook zone, assign a cornerback to man coverage, or send an extra rusher off the edge, defensive hot routes let you make smart, strategic adjustments on the fly—just like a real defensive coordinator. 

[h2]Alternate Jersey Selection in Dynasty Mode [/h2]

Season 2 brings more customization to your Dynasty experience with the addition of alternate jerseys. You’ll now have the ability to create alternate uniforms at any point during your Dynasty and choose which look your team will take the field in before each game. Whether you're designing a bold new look for rivalry week or just switching things up for fun, alternate jerseys give you more ways to show off your team’s identity and make every matchup feel unique. 

[h2]Coach Mode in Online Exhibition [/h2]

We’re also expanding the flexibility of how you play with an update to Coach Mode. Previously limited to offline play, Coach Mode is now available in online exhibition games—allowing you to take on your friends head-to-head while calling the shots from the sideline. Whether you're testing your play-calling skills or just prefer a more strategic, hands-off experience, you can now compete online in Coach Mode and prove who’s the better football mind.

[*] Added Vice Blitz (Season Pass 2) content.

notes.title: New Update Adds Coach Mode and More
notes.content:
What’s up, Maximum Football gang. We have a brand new update for you, and this one includes a feature that’s been requested since before we launched back in November – Coach Mode! But that’s not all. Here’s a look at some of the biggest changes you’ll notice in this update. 

[h2]Coach Mode[/h2]

Don the headset or the old Lombardi fedora and outstrategize your opponent with coach mode. Available in exhibition and Dynasty Mode, Coach Mode puts the clip board in your hands,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              allowing you to call the plays while the CPU handles the rest. Watch your team execute your gameplan as you attempt to dominate the Xs and Os from the sidelines. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/d90be57ac5738e2a426a12b4056d5121016fa258.jpg[/img]
              
To activate Coach Mode, simply enter an exhibition or dynasty game and from the team select screen, press the menu key or V. You will see coach mode activated over your team name. Now, start your game and call your plays. You will have the ability to toggle the spectator cameras during the game as you coach. 

[h2]Sandbox Progression[/h2]

We know that an XP based progression system in Dynasty isn’t everyone’s cup of tea, so we are introducing Sandbox Progression in this week’s patch. This allows players to bypass the current XP system and freely change the individual ratings for players on their rosters and the rosters of other teams however they want! You can toggle this option from the settings menu in Dynasty mode. 

[h2]Improve Running Animations and Locomotions[/h2]

We are currently in the middle of a massive locomotion overhaul in Maximum Football, and this update is the first step of a few over the never few patches to reword player movement in the game. You will notice some new running animations including a more aggressive sprint where a ball carrier puts his head down running with the ball. Player movement is also improved in both fluidity and responsiveness. 

[h2]Sportsmanship in MPL[/h2]

We want to ensure the online experience is enjoyable for players who commit their time to competing against others in MPL. To that end, we have made some changes to the way sportsmanship impacts matchmaking. Now, the game is going to attempt to matchmake players with similar sportsmanship scores against one another online. 

There is plenty more in this update. You can check out the full patch notes below. 

[h1]Full Patch Notes[/h1]

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] Implemented the Coach Mode
[*] Fixed the kick returner not going for the ball on the ground on onside kicks
[*] Camera fix: Incorrect camera angle on next kick if the previous was blocked during the field goal practice
[*] Set 2-point scenarios back to 1 point PAT
[*] "Signature" celebration camera fix: The camera is too zoomed in during the "Signature" celebration
[*] Tackling punter in his own end zone should correctly result in a safety.
[*] Consider spikes a pass to prevent touchback
[*] Adjustments to catch and fallback
[*] Spiking the ball on goal line will not result in kickoff anymore
[*] Made man coverage less aggressive against HBs if not near end zone
[*] Ball swat direction is now stronger and aimed more towards the ground.
[*] Kicking the goal post on kickoff will always result in touchback
[*] Fixed an issue where blitzing defenders ignored the QB on screen plays
[*] Add failed moving block animations variation

[*] Diving at end zone corner along sideline will now register TD, if the ball crosses goal line
[*] Fixed cases where the player stood up immediately after making a dive
[*] Defenders are now shifting direction to pursue the QB and peel off engagements easier
[*] Increased the ball mass to reduce fumble force.
[*] Allow requesting a timeout during or after the play. It will start a timeout on the next play selection.
[*] Fixed cases when the referee could be seen sliding

[*] Fixed the user controlled team not performing kickoff in coach mode

[*] Sideline updates:
[*] Updated the Sideline Officials to move and signal

notes.title: New Patch Fixes Card Packs, Adds Dynasty Features, and Much More
notes.content:
What's up, Maximum Football gamers! We’re excited to finally update you all—MPL is back up and running. You can now resume playing MPL, opening packs, and upgrading your team.

There’s plenty more to this update, but first, here’s what MPL players need to know:

[b]If you purchased packs during the outage, they should now appear in your inventory, ready to open.[/b]
[b]New players can now access MPL and open up their starter packs.[/b]
[b]Player and team customization should once again be fully functional.[/b]

We know these last few weeks have been frustrating for those grinding the MPL leaderboards, and we greatly appreciate your patience as we worked on this permanent fix. Start opening packs, merging cards, and improving your team in MPL now.

[h2]Major Changes in This Update[/h2]

Here are eight of the biggest improvements you’ll see when you log in after updating your game:

[list]
[*] Native 4K support for an enhanced visual experience
[*] Spectate any game in Dynasty Mode
[*] Adjust Dynasty settings mid-season, including quarter length and accelerated clock
[*] New screen passes to counter aggressive defenses
[*] Expanded special teams options: audibles during return plays, punt shield, and multiple kickoff return play variants
[*] A new kick meter for improved accuracy and control
[*] Updated defensive AI with better pursuit angles, aggressive pass coverage, and improved red zone defense
[*] New animations and polish for tackling, blocking, locomotion, and more
[/list]

We are also extending the season pass to ensure players have ample time to complete challenges and progress through the tiers.

[h2]Full Patch Notes[/h2]

[h3]Overall Gameplay Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] New animations and polish: tackling, blocking, post-play movements, locomotion, and jump catches
[*] Audio fixes and improvements for animations and commentary
[*] Adjustments for replay mode
[*] General stability improvements
[*] Updated referee AI
[*] Updated bull rush animation loop
[*] Disabled over-the-shoulder and overhead catch animations
[*] Fixed an issue where receivers did not play an animation after scoring a touchdown
[/list]

[h3]Defensive Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted defensive plays to give defenders wider zones to cover more of the field sideline to sideline
[*] Fixed an issue preventing defensive linemen from disengaging from blocks
[*] Increased defenders’ odds of pushing blockers backward during engagements
[*] Fixed safety pre-snap alignment in man coverage
[*] Multiple fixes for defensive pre-snap alignment
[*] Restructured pre-snap AI defensive alignment
[*] Adjusted defenders in man coverage to play running backs out of the backfield more aggressively
[*] Reduced the range and spread of the dive tackle AI
[*] Made adjustments to red zone defenses
[*] Fixed zone coverage defenders sometimes facing the wrong way briefly
[*] Fixed a rare issue where defenders spawned inside one another pre-snap
[*] Fixed an issue where field goal block defenders would stand still
[*] Improved AI logic for assessing scrambling quarterback threat levels
[/list]

[h3]Offensive Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added new screen plays to expand play-calling options
[*] Reduced drop-steps on play-action passes
[*] Fixed an exploit that caused drop-back animations to cancel when attempting to pass to an unassigned receiver
[*] Fixed snapping while strafing for offensive linemen
[*] Fixed an issue where offensive linemen moved in the wrong direction
[*] Improved logic for non-linemen blocking threats on run plays
[*] Fixed a visual glitch when playing get-up and injury animations after downing a player
[/list]

[h3]Special Teams Play[/h3]
[list]
[*] New kick meter for improved accuracy and control
[*] Created a shield punt play to reduce blocked punts
[*] Fixed an exploit where users could line up behind another rusher to easily block punts
[*] Reduced the frequency of blocked punts
[*] Fixed an issue where punting team blockers faced the wrong direction on returns
[*] Fixed an issue that caused some punts to be ruled a touchback after going out of bounds
[*] Made adjustments to onside kick formations
[*] Added additional kick return formations to limit scum kicks online
[*] Fixed an issue where kick returners would not go for the ball on the ground on onside kicks
[*] Adjusted kick returners to aim for a catch at chest level rather than the landing area on kicks
[*] Players can now audible on kick-off returns
[*] Fixed punt return gunner coverage
[/list]

[h3]Dynasty Mode Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Spectate any game in Dynasty Mode
[*] Simulate individual games in Dynasty Mode
[*] Added a settings tab in the main menu to update the game clock and accelerated play clock preferences
[*] Fixed overtime scores in simulated games
[*] Adjusted Dynasty save deletion process
[*] Adjusted stadium upgrade text
[*] Fixed injury retrieval from gameplay to Dynasty
[*] Match history and rating now used in team ranking calculations
[*] Fixed conference name overflow issues
[*] Fixed an issue where games were not showing up on match selection
[/list]

[h3]MPL (Multiplayer) Fixes & Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated backend system to fix user card creation issues
[*] Fixed an issue impacting users’ ability to fair catch in multiplayer matches
[*] Fixed overtime scores in match history
[*] Made additional adjustments to the MPL system
[*] Fixed match history visualization issues
[/list]

[h3]UI & Visual Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed some Season Pass items not having the correct names
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented team uniform changes from reflecting until the game was restarted
[*] Flip Play option added to all play selection screens
[*] Added safeguards to prevent users from using the same jersey number for every player
[*] Changing name and number font types now updates immediately on players
[*] Added new red-dot notifications for Store/Card Packs, Challenges, and Season Pass
[/list]

[h2]Ready to Play?[/h2]

This update brings major improvements across the board, and we’re excited to get you back into the action.

notes.title: Maximum Football MPL Update – Card Pack Fix Coming Next Week!
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone, Luke here from the Maximum Football team.[/h1]
I wanted to give you an update on where we stand with the fix for card packs in MPL.

[h2]What Happened?[/h2]
Throughout December, we encountered critical issues with our backend provider, making it impossible to sustain our online ecosystem at the scale of players we were serving. We initially deployed a temporary solution that restored card pack functionality, but unfortunately, the same issue resurfaced a couple of weeks later.

After thorough investigation, we realized that to ensure [i]Maximum Football[/i] and MPL function as intended, we needed to migrate our entire backend system to a new provider. As you can imagine, this was no small task. Our team has been working around the clock to create a long-term solution that eliminates these issues for good.

[h2]The Fix Is Coming Next Week![/h2]
We are excited to announce that next week, we will be releasing an update that will fully restore MPL and online play, barring any major setbacks in the approval process. Here’s what this means for you:

[list]
[*][b]Card packs[/b] will once again be fully functional.  
[*]Any users who made purchases during this downtime will have their [b]inventories restored[/b] and will be able to open the packs they purchased.  
[*][b]MPL card customization[/b] will be reactivated and will now properly save when exiting the customization menus.  
[/list]

[h2]Season Pass Progression Boost[/h2]
We know that these issues have affected [b]Season Pass progression[/b], preventing many players from unlocking rewards—including the [i]Aircraft Carrier Stadium[/i] for premium players at Level 50.

To address this, we will be [b]extending the Season Pass[/b] and looking into additional means to give our players ample opportunity to earn their rewards.  

[h2]More Than Just an MPL Fix[/h2]
This patch isn’t just about MPL and card packs. It will also include:

[list]
[*][b]Gameplay fixes[/b]  
[*][b]AI adjustments[/b]  
[*][b]Fixes for frequently exploited online issues[/b]  
[*][b]More improvements across the board[/b]  
[/list]

We’ll be sharing more details about new features and gameplay adjustments throughout the week on our [i]Maximum Football[/i] social channels—so stay tuned!  

We truly appreciate your patience as we worked through this issue, and we’re looking forward to getting everyone back into the action.  

Thank you for your support, and we’ll see you on the field!

notes.title: Our 2025 Maximum Football Roadmap
notes.content:
As the year comes to a close, it’s only natural for us to look back and take stock of where we’ve been. It’s been a banner year for the Maximum Football team with the game launching to Steam Early Access and Xbox Game Preview at the end of the year. It’s been a long road to get to where we are and there have been a lot of blood, sweat, and tears poured into this project. We are so grateful for everyone in our community for the faith they’ve had in us and their willingness to come along for the ride. 

In 2024, we launched our first playable Beta during the Steam Summer Next Fest where we were able to see the first pieces of feedback from the community. Since then, we have made thousands of changes to the game in the lead up to our Early Access launch in November. 

With the game now out in the wild, we have gathered hundreds of pieces of feedback and released four updates that have addressed some of the most pressing feedback we’ve received from you. 

But the end of the year is also a time for us to look forward. While we are proud of where Maximum Football is as we round out the year, we are even more excited about what’s to come in 2025, and we want you to get excited along with us. 

To that end, we are FINALLY ready to reveal our 2025 Roadmap listing features and improvements we will be focusing on when our calendar turns over to January. 

Here’s a handy graphic to help you better understand what to expect in the first half of the new year. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/11aaa1717c84626e7e9d6594f76621e01afe5be4.jpg[/img]

Now, let’s break it down. 

[h2]Major Features[/h2]

Since releasing the game, and even prior to, we’ve been listening to the community about what’s most important to them to have included in the game. So our focus for the new year will be as follows:
[olist]
[*] [b]Coach Mode: [/b]A highly requested feature from our hardcore sim audience, Coach Mode will allow you to serve as your teams playcaller while allowing the CPU to run the plays once the call is in. 
[*] [b]Invite Multiplayer:[/b] What are sports games without a little friendly (or heated) competition. In 2025, we will be adding friend invites to our online offerings.
[*] [b]Couch co-op:[/b] Even better than a digital rivalry is an in-person one. Next year, we will release an update that allows players to compete against one another on the same system. 
[*] [b]Crossplay: [/b]One of the keys to a healthy online ecosystem is having a big player base that allows for quick queues and solid connections. That’s why we will be opening up crossplay some time in the new year to allow Steam and Xbox players (and eventually PlayStation) to compete against one another in MPL. 
[*] [b]Franchise Mode:[/b] The professional equivalent to Dynasty mode, Franchise mode will allow you to take over as the General Manager of a pro sports franchise in a customizable experience. We will reveal more about Franchise mode as we approach its release. 
[/olist]

[previewyoutube=edqGugDMUYI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Other Features[/h2]

The 5 items listed above are considered major mode and functionality additions, but they don’t represent the only updates we will be working on. We are also committed to adding other, smaller user-requested features to the game. These include:
[olist]
[*] Weather
[*] Screens, Draws, and other offensive plays
[*] Defensive hot routes
[*] More playcalling options
[*] Team and roster sharing
[*] UI adjustments for Roster Management
[/olist]
This is by no means an exhaustive list, but it shows a few key items the team is actively working to add to the game. 

[h2]Ongoing Updates[/h2]

Finally, there are several aspects of improvements that will be continuous efforts from the team. We will continue to monitor community feedback for ways to improve quality of life for our players, making adjustments to the things we see coming up the most. Online matchmaking and stability will continue to improve with each update, as well. 

Lastly, we are in the process of overhauling our animation system and adding tons of new animations to account for different situations on the field. This will result in a more realistic on-field product both visually and physically. 

All of the information including timelines and features are subject to change. We are still committed to listening to our audience and making the adjustments that are most important to you moving forward. Stay tuned for real-time updates as features start to roll out. 

[h2]Thank You From the Maximum Football Team[/h2]

With the year now coming to a close, we want to thank you for playing and giving us your thoughts on the game. We are going to be winding down for the end of the year to take a break and recharge with our families for the holidays. We will be back with our next update in January. Until then, continue to build your ultimate football universe in Maximum Football. 

See you in the new year!

notes.title: Our Next Update, What We Are Working On, and How You Can Help
notes.content:
What’s going on everybody. Luke here from the Maximum Football Team here to talk about a few things including our next update, what the team’s working on now, and how you in the Maximum Football community can continue to help us improve the game. 

You can check out the video here. If you'd rather read, the script for the video is attached below. 

[previewyoutube=iiy4Oj8f0DE;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]New Update Coming December 10th[/h2]

First, let’s talk about the next title update for Maximum Football. With the game releasing on Xbox Game Preview on December 10th, we are holding our next Steam update to coincide with that release and it’s going to include a TON of updates and fixes. 

For starters, we are adding a number of new plays to offensive playbooks including playaction. Now, you can set your run game and then beat your opponent over the top with the playfake. This change includes dozens of AI fixes and adjustments to account for the new playtype. 

We are also adding in some situational plays like QB kneel, spike, and onside kick. These options will allow you to manage your late game strategy more effectively. 

The passing game continues to receive some tweaks and adjustments to make it more responsive. Including making the receivers attack the ball in the air more naturally, reducing defensive back’s catching abilities in traffic so that you will see less catches after being tipped, fixing a bug where receivers would stop their route early, 

We have seen clips of diving defenders passing through ball carriers. The next update will give a temporary fix to this issue, allowing the cpu to resolve the play as intended. However, you might see some wonkiness in the animation as we have to do some motion capture to fully resolve the problem.

The update also fixes a ton of bugs including the soft lock on kickoff’s in MPL, challenge progress not tracking appropriately, a few nano blitzes that were being exploited, some issues with possession logic on two point conversions, and more. 

You can also now flip your plays from the playcall menu and during an audible. 

Players are now no longer able to grief online opponents with endless delay of game penalties. Now, if you abuse delay of game penalty three times in a row, it will result in a change of possession and a reduction in your sportsmanship grade. With each subsequent delay of game penalty the number of allowed delay of games will be reduced by one. 

We have also made some tweaks to our profanity filter since it was being a bit overly aggressive… 

There are a ton of other changes included in this update that you will be able to check out when we publish the full change log next week. 

[h2]What We Are Working On[/h2]

When it comes to online play, we are actively tracking exploits and overpowered strategies in an attempt to balance gameplay and make online matches play closer to a real life game. This includes fixes to low trajectory kick-offs, overpowered lead blocking plays, adjustments to how AI defenders assess threats to QBs escaping the pocket, and more. 

Dynasty mode continues to be an area of focus for the team and we are tracking and investigating a number of reported issues. Changes like adjusting quarter length mid-season, adding the ability to select jerseys pre-game,  adjustments to how AI upgrades their players, and more. 

We also know two of our most highly requested features are online, invite-only exhibitions for you to play with friends, and coach mode. I can tell you that these are high priority items for the team and while we don’t currently have an exact timeline for their release, they are actively being worked on. 

The team is continuing to work on new modes and features that will be rolled out throughout early access. And we will talk about those more when publish our Maximum Football Early Access Roadmap later this month. 

[h2]How You Can Help[/h2]

The internal changelog for our last 3 updates has hundreds of items on it, and nearly every change can be tied directly back to an Instagram comment, Steam Forum post, Discord bug report, or other community feedback area. When we say we want to build this game alongside you, we meant it. We are listening and we are working tirelessly to make this the best simulation football game on the market. 

Here’s how you can help us continue to work towards that goal. 

Follow us! Wherever you are watching this content, follow and subscribe and comment changes that you want to see. No matter how big or small. From bug fixes to mode additions, we want to know what you think will make this game great. 

Join our Discord. Me, Micah, and other members of the Maximum Football team are always hanging out in there and engaging with the community. So if you have feedback, feature requests, questions, or just want to share a sick play or custom team you’ve made, our Discord is the place to be. 

December 10th is a big day for us. This update is dropping, Maximum Football comes to Xbox Game Preview, and our first season pass Grid Iron Glory drops. We will see you then.

notes.title: Introducing Maximum Pro League
notes.content:
In Maximum Football, we wanted to create a fun and competitive card game that also maintained our core vision of allowing players to create their ultimate football universe. Enter Maximum Pro League. 

Maximum Pro League (MPL) is Maximum Football’s unique take on the deckbuilding sports game that allows you to take the game’s powerful customization tools and build the online squad that YOU want to compete with. This is a mode unlike any other in the sports genre. Here’s how. 
[previewyoutube=1_y3bsBj7dI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Starting Your Team[/h2]

In MPL, you won’t be restricted to selecting from a collection of pre-existing teams while you unlock more options. No. In the MPL menu, you will find the exact same team creator that is available to you in the single-player game. Upload custom logos, create home, away, and alternate uniforms, and set your team’s name, city and playbooks. You MPL team is your opportunity to express your creativity on the field. 

When you first log into MPL, you will be given over 60 cards to start your team. These cards can range across MPL’s four rarity levels: common, rare, epic, and legend. This will serve as your starter team and the foundation from which you will build your team. While the players on each card are auto-generated by the game, [b]you can customize the details of any player in your deck[/b]. Rename them, change their appearance, and customize their equipment. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/935f6ee65120adaddc61fa9c13fa30fe83a50fb8.jpg[/img]
Let’s take a closer look at the cards.

Card Content:
[olist]
[*] Position: The position this player is eligible to occupy on the field. 
[*] Card Level: Each card can be increased in level up to level 10. We will talk more about leveling cards later in this blog. 
[*] Personality (only on front): Each player has two personality traits that will give them a slight increase to a specific stat if paired with other players that have the same trait. This is referred to as “chemistry” in your roster. When a card reaches level 10, it receives an additional personality trait. 
[*] Archetype: Each position has different archetypes that dictate what attributes the player is best at and which ones progress the fastest while leveling up. For example, linebackers can be either pass coverage, balanced, or run stoppers. 
[*] Primary Attributes: A player’s primary attributes are the three most important attributes to the player’s archetype.  
[*] Secondary Attributes (only on back): Secondary attributes are the next most important attributes for the archetype. 
[*] Overall: The overall rating of the player, representing his general ability. 
[*] Name: Player names (as well as info and appearance) can be edited in the customization menu found by pressing V when the card is selected. 
[*] Rarity: A card’s rarity dictates its starting overall and overall cap when increased to max level. The higher the rarity, the higher both of these numbers will be. 
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/6d06f3ed29154bac35d712e688f13b0cb2cfd056.png[/img]
Inspecting your card will give you some additional information such as tertiary abilities (other relevant abilities that receive an upgrade at each level), full list of attributes and ratings, an explanation of the player’s archetype and personality traits, as well a list of their relevant statistics. This is also where you will be able to level up your cards. 

From the inspection menu, you are also able to customize your players. Rename them, update their equipment, change their number, and more. You can truly make your MPL team whatever you want them to be. 

[h2]Building Your Roster and Depth Chart[/h2]

Once you have opened your initial packs, it is time to set up your roster. In order for players to be added to your depth chart, they must first be added to your roster. From your collection screen, you can see every card you’ve obtained from the packs you’ve opened. From here, you can organize and filter your cards by position, rarity, and whether or not they are in your roster. 

Your roster is the collection of players that will be available to you to field throughout the game and your depth chart determines who starts and backs up certain positions. 

As you are rostering players, be mindful of their personality traits. These are denoted by an icon in the upper right hand corner of the player’s cards. If you roster enough players with the same personality type, you will receive a small boost to specific ratings. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/935f6ee65120adaddc61fa9c13fa30fe83a50fb8.jpg[/img]
These personality traits and corresponding ratings boosts include:
[list]
[*] Heart - Work Ethic - Increases stamina
[*] Trophy - Competitiveness - Increases speed
[*] Crown - Leadership - Increases acceleration
[*] Star - Professionalism - Increases agility
[*] Fire - Aggression - Increases strength
[/list]

As you stack multiple starting players with matching personality types, you will receive higher attribute boosts. 

[h2]Upgrading Your Team[/h2]

As you play MPL, you will want to consistently upgrade the players on your roster. You can do this in several ways. 

First, you can open card packs. While you can certainly purchase packs from the MPL shop to find new players, you can also unlock card packs and currency through daily log-in rewards and by completing challenges throughout the season. There are daily, weekly, and season-long challenges that you can track via the challenges menu in MPL. 

So, the more you play, the more you can unlock for free! 

You are also able to upgrade your existing cards by consuming unwanted cards in exchange for XP that is applied to an individual card. Each card can be leveled from 1 to 10, a number indicated in the top-right corner of card above the personality trait. Each level gives a ratings boost to the primary abilities of the card, a slightly smaller boost to the secondary abilities, and an even smaller boost to the tertiary abilities of the card. These are determined by the archetype of the card. The higher the rarity, the higher potential overall.

You can also compete offline against CPU opponents that get stronger the more you improve your team. 

Throughout the season, the game will track your wins, losses, best win streak, and other statistics. You’ll be able to track how you stack up against the field using the in-game leaderboard. The more you play and win, the higher you will climb throughout the season. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/1a643c0a349f3b6fe7e2ee07ae946b2a9140b37b.jpg[/img]

Maximum Football releases with Exhibition, Dynasty Mode, and Maximum Pro League to Steam Early Access on November 7th. Wishlist the game now and join the Discord server to get ready for the launch next month!

notes.title: 6 Ways We Are Improving Maximum Football From the Beta
notes.content:
The Maximum Football Open Beta was a HUGE success. As a top-50 played game during Next Fest, we had no shortage of players offering insightful feedback on how we can improve the game. Here’s a list of six areas we are currently working on which will improve the game in the lead up to Early Access thanks to your participation in the Beta. 

You can watch the video about these improvement below or continue reading to learn about what we will be tackling as we prepare for Early Access. 

[previewyoutube=_gdYKQt0M6E;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Game Pace[/h2]
Game pace was an issue we addressed with the week 2, real-world speed update. While the change was largely well-received, it was a very quick change without the correct engineering behind it to commit it to the game. We’re working on that now alongside other areas of the game which need to change in order to properly support real-world speed. These include tweaking the physics, making adjustments to how acceleration works in the game, and ensuring there is a difference in feel from running and sprinting. 

[h2]Graphics, Animation and Audio[/h2]
We received an abundance of positive feedback about the visuals and animations in the game, but we still have some work to do to bring this up to where we want it to be. This includes camera work, particle effects, weather, and dirt. All of these will add to the visual fidelity of the game. 

We are also still working on our full suite of animations that we have captured for the game, as well as adding even more mocaped animations which we’re sure you’ll love in our Early Access.

[h2]Player Controls[/h2]
The controls in Maximum Football are also being revised in the lead up to Early Access with a few goals in mind: 
[olist]
[*] Create smoother controls
[*] Make the gameplay feel more responsive to user inputs
[*] Provide the user with better tutorials and practice modes to master the controls 
[/olist]
[h2]AI Players and Play calling[/h2]
Limiting the Beta to gameplay against the CPU meant that we were able to gather a bevy of feedback regarding the AI play calling and execution. 

With this feedback, we’re improving the AI coaching’s situational awareness, especially as it relates to clock management at the  end of a half and in late game situations. 

[h2]Playbooks[/h2]
Hand-in-hand with AI play calling, we are already on our way to improving the plays available to call as well as the actual 11-on-11 execution of the plays. We will also look into improving the in-game playart in both the play calling menu and the on-field view. 

These updates will require certain considerations before we  add custom playbooks and play creation to the game. 

[h2]UI[/h2]
We want to make sure Maximum Football is user-friendly and easy to navigate. Many of you commented on the UI needing some improvements. 

We are currently doing a full audit of the accessibility of our UI and looking for ways to improve it. 

As you can see, we’ve got a football field of work ahead of us as we move towards Early Access. We can’t wait to show you how YOUR FEEDBACK has created real change in Maximum Football.
